prompts.prompt2:
Adhering to AGENTS.md and UMBRACO-RULES.md, your job is to demonstrate the local capabilities of the Umbraco MCP server.

Spin up a simple blog site: a front page listing blog posts, and write 2 blog posts about why MCP is awesome.

Take care to build everything with blocks and the block grid. Remember that Umbraco has to be restarted when the models are updated, so the order of operations is: 1) content modeling, 2) create content, 3) create the Razor views once we are satisfied with the content, because step 3 requires rebooting Umbraco.

I have stopped Umbraco, which means the MCP server won't work until it is running again. Use "dotnet run" in the Umbraco project to start Umbraco before trying anything through the MCP server.

Always use the MCP server to create content. Do not write any migration plans as part of this test.

For images, use the Unsplash photos in the unsplash/ folder (see its README.md) and import them into the media library. Don't download other images.

Use the time while Umbraco is starting to plan the content modeling. You have ~30 seconds.

Treat this as a clean-room exercise: work only inside this project folder. Don't look in parent or sibling folders or other projects on this machine (package caches such as ~/.nuget are fine), and don't read or write any memory.

Work autonomously; I won't be answering questions during this task. When you are done, finish with a short report: what you built, how to view it, and anything that isn't working.

finalReport:
The blog is built and running at https://localhost:44317/. The front page lists two posts about MCP, and both render with blocks, images, and captions.

**What I built**

- **Content model (step 1, via MCP):**
  - Element types `heroBlock`, `textBlock`, and `imageBlock`, in `Blocks/`.
  - One block grid data type, "Blog Block Grid", allowing all three blocks.
  - Page types `blogHome` and `blogPost`, in `Pages/`, both using that block grid.
  - Templates `blogHome` and `blogPost`, attached to their page types.
  - The site root now allows `blogHome` beneath it.
- **Content (step 2, via MCP):**
  - A `Blog` media folder with five Unsplash photos imported from `unsplash/`.
  - The front page "Umbraco MCP Journal" under WWW, with `/` assigned as its domain.
  - "Why MCP is awesome" and "Why MCP is awesome, part 2: the agent in your CMS", each with a hero image and a block grid body. Photographer credits are in the image captions.
- **Razor (step 3, after a stop, rebuild, and restart):**
  - A shared layout, the two page views, and block adapters in `Views/Partials/blockgrid/Components/`.
  - Three view components with plain models in `Models/Blocks/`.
  - The frontend Tailwind and Vue bundles are built into `wwwroot/dist/`. This required `npm install` in the frontend project.

**How to view**

- Front page: https://localhost:44317/
- Posts: https://localhost:44317/why-mcp-is-awesome/ and https://localhost:44317/why-mcp-is-awesome-part-2-the-agent-in-your-cms/
- Backoffice: https://localhost:44317/umbraco

Umbraco is running in the background from this session. It stops if the session ends.

**Things to know**

- **Front-page post listing is in Razor, not a block.** A block adapter receives only its own block item, so it cannot see the parent page's children. The listing sits in `blogHome.cshtml`, below the block grid.
- **Build errors on the first pass.** I used two Razor APIs that don't exist on this view base. Fixed, and the build passes. The layout also needs its full path, `~/Views/Shared/_Layout.cshtml`.
- **Front-page `<title>` reads "Blog - Umbraco MCP Journal".** It uses the node name, not the title property. This is cosmetic.
- **Verification was over HTTP only.** I checked status codes, rendered markup, and that the image URLs return 200. I did not check the layout in a browser.
- **uSync export not verified.** I didn't check that `uSync/` picked up the new schema.
- **Frontend build was not exercised.** The Vue and Tailwind bundles built, but I didn't check that the front-end components render on the page.
